How Does Fox News Frame the WNBA?

Analyzing the right-wing politicization of the Women’s National Basketball Association

Since I moved to Seattle five years ago, I’ve become a big WNBA fan. (Let’s go, Storm.) I’ve also become fixated on a question. Why is Fox News obsessed with the WNBA?

This question dawned on me slowly, especially since I don’t read or watch Fox News.

The first clue: my web browser. As I started reading more WNBA news, my Google Chrome app recommended more WNBA news. That made sense. But then I started getting served coverage from, of all places, Fox News.

Wait, what?

It wasn’t just one article, either. I saw dozens of Fox News takes on women’s basketball, often with a clear political bias, and an implicitly racist and homophobic framing.

Headline after headline pitted the league’s most famous straight white star, Caitlin Clark, against other WNBA players, mainly Black and/or queer women, like Alyssa Thomas, DiJonai Carrington, or Angel Reese.

FOX NEWS June 2026

Who is Alyssa Thomas? WNBA star suspended for punching Caitlin Clark in the throat

FOX NEWS January 2025

WNBA star who hurt Caitlin Clark's eye calls for league to take action against Trump administration policies

FOX NEWS May 2025

Dave Portnoy calls Angel Reese a jacka-- for jealousy of Caitlin Clark in response to ESPN analyst

FOX NEWS July 2026

CNN's Abby Phillip claims GOP lawmakers back Caitlin Clark exclusively because she is White

I knew it was being talked about on their TV programs, too.

At a holiday gathering, I was chatting with an older conservative family member, who, out of the blue, started name-dropping WNBA players—saying praiseworthy things about Caitlin Clark and suspect things about other Black players, including Brittney Griner.

This person has never seen a WNBA game in their life. But they do mainline Fox News on cable TV.

The right-wing politicization of the WNBA burst into the mainstream in the summer of 2026. In July, Fever shooting guard Sophie Cunningham made openly anti-trans remarks, which inspired right-wing politicians and anti-trans advocates around the world to rally around her—including Vice President J.D. Vance and J.K. Rowling.

Even Fox News political pundits are confused and exhausted by the WNBA coverage. As Jesse Watters recently said on air: “We have to do this again, really? Someone wore a t-shirt at a WNBA game? This isn’t a news story…. We don’t even cover the NBA. Why are we covering the WNBA?”

How did professional women’s basketball—a league that, for decades, most people didn’t watch or care anything about—transform into a mainstream political lightning rod?

Well, it didn’t happen overnight. And, undeniably, the media played a role.

So I decided to collect some data and analyze the media’s role—especially Fox News—in framing the WNBA as a hot-button culture war conversation that was primed, at the right moment, to explode.

Finding the data

First, I collected any Fox News article that mentioned the WNBA or its players over the past six years. That came to 2,153 articles, published between July 2019 and August 2026.

In 2021, Fox acquired Outkick, a website that features sports commentary from a conservative perspective. They claim to be “the antidote to the mainstream sports media that often serves an elite, left-leaning minority,” dedicated to “questioning the consensus and exposing the destructive nature of ‘woke’ activism.” Many of Fox News’s sports articles come from Outkick and are published through their site.

Additionally, I gathered nine years worth of cable news chyrons. You know, those headlines that appear at the bottom of your screen, like so:

This data came from the Internet Archive's Third Eye OCR feed, which Charlie Smart used in a previous very cool analysis of political news bias.

To provide a comparison, I also collected coverage from MSNBC, CNN, Yahoo Sports, ESPN, and CBS Sports.

Lopsided Coverage, and a “Bad Deal”

For most of its history, Fox News barely covered the WNBA. They talked about the NBA much more.

But you can see that coverage clearly surges in the “Caitlin Clark era”—that is, after Clark was drafted into the league in April 2024.

Mentions of Caitlin Clark in Fox WNBA articles

Before Clark, though, there was another WNBA main character: Brittney Griner. Griner’s story is important for understanding the nature of Fox News’s coverage and the political narratives they have historically used to frame women’s basketball players.

Mentions of Brittney Griner in Fox WNBA articles

In 2022, Griner was arrested by Russian officials for possession of marijuana and detained for nearly a year. She had been playing in Russia during the WNBA offseason—something many players did to supplement their shamefully low salaries. After a trial, she was sentenced to nine years in prison. Luckily, at the end of 2022, she was released in a prisoner swap.

All three networks — MSNBC, CNN, and Fox — covered the saga extensively. Fox actually covered it less than the other two. But when they did discuss or feature the prisoner swap, they framed things in a particular way—as a bad deal.

This is every word in the three networks’ cable coverage of the WNBA, via their chyrons.

While MSNBC named the man Griner was exchanged for, Viktor Bout…

Fox New mostly used his moniker: The Merchant of Death.

By dramatizing his danger, they reinforced the idea that Griner’s swap was a bad deal.

In their online news coverage, they said as much.

FOX NEWS July 2022

Trump: Brittney Griner prisoner swap for 'Merchant of Death' doesn't seem like a very good trade

FOX NEWS December 2022

Trump: White House 'not going to apologize' for releasing 'Merchant of Death' as critics rail 'bad deal'

In other words, they devalued Griner’s life. After her release, Fox framed Griner as unpatriotic, emphasized her masculinity and non-normative gender choices, and platformed activists who condemned her support of trans women in sports.

FOX NEWS December 2022

Brittney Griner is coming home. Will she stand for the anthem now that she's back in the USA?

FOX NEWS July 2024

WNBA star Brittney Griner plans to have child call her ‘pops’

FOX NEWS April 2023

Riley Gaines calls Brittney Griner's remarks on transgender athlete participation ‘heartbreaking’

It is no coincidence that Griner is also a politically outspoken queer Black woman. Her treatment provides a window into Fox News’s framing of the WNBA overall, a league that includes many Black and queer women, and one that has been defined by a history of activism, which Fox News often opposed.

The WNBA’s Political Activism

In 2020, WNBA players engaged in highly visible protest in support of the Black Lives Matter movement.

They walked off the court during the national anthem, wore BLM and “Say Her Name” shirts on national television, and successfully campaigned to unseat a team owner who sat in the U.S. Senate, Kelly Loeffler, after she opposed players’ activism.

Increasingly, they also spotlighted the league’s LGBTQ+ players and related issues, including trans rights and trans women’s participation in sports.

In spring 2023, Megan Rapinoe and Sue Bird signed a letter opposing a bill restricting transgender athletes, and Brittney Griner backed trans participation in sports.

FOX NEWS April 2023

Megan Rapinoe, Sue Bird among athletes who sign letter opposing Protection of Girls and Women in Sports Act

FOX NEWS April 2023

Brittney Griner backs transgender participation in sports: ‘A crime’ to ‘separate someone for any reason’

In response, Fox News platformed swimmer and anti-trans advocate Riley Gaines, who called Griner’s remarks “heartbreaking,” as well as former NBA player Enes Kanter, who suggested that if trans women were allowed to join the WNBA, he would, too. This is a hateful stunt that he has revived in 2026.

FOX NEWS April 2023

Riley Gaines calls Brittney Griner's remarks on transgender athlete participation ‘heartbreaking’

FOX NEWS August 2023

Enes Freedom on trans athletes in women's sports: ‘Should I put on a wig ... and start dominating the WNBA?’

Then, in 2024, Caitlin Clark arrived. And the culture war WNBA conversation heated up even more.

Enter Caitlin Clark

Caitlin Clark, the three-point phenom from Iowa, was drafted #1 by the Indiana Fever in 2024. Her popularity has drawn millions of new viewers and fans to the league. But it has also launched the WNBA into a culture war/identity politics debate that often has little to do with the league itself.

Many commentators have noted that Clark’s background as a straight, white, Midwestern star may play a role in her broad appeal. It is undeniable that Clark has drawn in a whiter, more conservative, and more mainstream audience than the WNBA—a historically Black and queer league—has had in the past.

Fox News has been obsessed with dispelling the identity-related dimension of this narrative. At the same time, Fox News has played up Clark’s treatment in the league, specifically hard fouls committed against her, often in implicitly racialized terms that malign the Black and/or queer players who committed the fouls.

Case in point: Fox News has consistently discussed “hard” fouls against Caitlin Clark more than other outlets.

They also invoked race and racism more than other outlets, as well as culture war buzzwords like “privilege.”

Here’s every word in both archives. Switch between whole articles and headlines, or filter to Caitlin Clark alone.

As Seerhat Sohi has written, it’s important to acknowledge the real physicality that Clark has faced in the league, and to demand improvements to refereeing across the board. This is especially true because trolls “will just use this controversy to denigrate the rest of the WNBA. “No amount of good PR,” she warns, “is going to stop clickbait or the right’s obsession with criticizing the WNBA.”

Overall, Fox News only discusses Caitlin Clark slightly more than other outlets.

But they discuss players like DiJonai Carrington—who have committed fouls against Caitlin Clark, and who also have outspoken views against the Trump administration—much more.

And they discuss comparable stars like Paige Bueckers, Napheesa Collier, and A’ja Wilson much less.

Every player, and the outlet picker: set Fox against Yahoo, ESPN, CBS or USA Today on its own.

The Fox News-WNBA Expanded Universe

This leads us to consider the cast of characters who are spotlighted in WNBA coverage, including people who are not directly connected to the league.

Fox News often speaks the most loudly and politically through the individuals they platform, using them as mouthpieces.

Additionally, they pit players against each other in ways that amplify divisive political narratives.

Fox News WNBA headlines, 2019–2023

and
WNBA players & leagueright-leaning voicesleft-leaning voicesno clear lean

Hover a face for their headlines · click to pin them, click a second to see only what they share · drag to rearrange

Each face is someone Fox News named in a WNBA headline. A line means two of them shared a headline.

For example, in 2022, when Brittney Griner is detained in Russia, a headline mentions Griner, Joe Biden, Paul Whelan, and Viktor Bout.

In 2023, Fox News platforms two anti-trans advocates who have no direct connection to the WNBA.

When Clark arrives, Fox News constantly pits her against Angel Reese, and they share 50 headlines.

Once again, Fox News turns to reliable cast members like Barstool's Dave Portnoy to provide a spin.

By 2026 the network is dense, and some of the loudest nodes are not even in the league: Riley Gaines, Dave Portnoy, Enes Kanter, J.K. Rowling.

Trans Women in Sports

Fox News consistently fanned the flames of the WNBA culture war. They denied that race, sexuality, or gender were relevant considerations in the league, yet foregrounded them more than any other outlet.

The implicit misogyny, and suspicion of “social justice” and queer communities, laid the groundwork for the right-wing, anti-trans movement to rise up and seize the WNBA as a central issue—even though no trans women currently even play in the league.

Fox WNBA articles about trans athletes

Fox WNBA articles per month that mention trans athletes or eligibility in women’s sports. Source: Fox News.

Through 2025, Fox planted the seed for controversy around trans issues and the WNBA, discussing it periodically but consistently.

Then, in 2026, it exploded.

And as a share of everything Fox writes about the WNBA, trans coverage went from a sliver to the majority: in August 2026, nearly two out of every three Fox WNBA articles mention trans athletes.

Anti-trans rhetoric

Share of Fox WNBA articles each month containing trans language (“trans,” “transgender,” or “biological males”) or “protect” — as in “protecting women’s sports” — smoothed with a 5-month window.

Among the TV networks, Fox News talks about trans issues way more than the others.

As Jesse Watters recently said on air, “Why are we covering the WNBA?” Or, more pointedly, “This is something I don’t care about.” Watters said the quiet part out loud. Fox News doesn’t actually care about women’s basketball. Right-wing pundits and politicians are using the WNBA to push their own agenda.

Sports are political. They have always been political. Throughout American history, athletes have been able to use their platform to advocate for justice. Players in the WNBA are a great example. But we should be wary of how narratives about the WNBA are being framed by the right-wing media and outside parties who have little to no actual investment in the league.

When I went to my first WNBA game, I was shocked by how inclusive it felt. It was completely different from every other (men’s) professional sporting event I had ever been to. The version of the WNBA presented by Fox News is not recognizable to me. We need to recognize this framing—and push back against it—lest we all get played.

Data and Methods

The articles: every WNBA article I could collect from Fox News, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Just Women’s Sports, The Athletic, CBS Sports, and USA Today, 2019–2026—plus Fox’s NBA coverage as a control. Fox, ESPN, Yahoo, and Just Women’s Sports include full article text; The Athletic, CBS Sports, and USA Today are headlines only.

The chyrons: nine years of cable news chyrons—the banner text at the bottom of the screen—from Fox News, CNN, and MSNBC, via the Internet Archive’s Third Eye project.

The word comparisons use weighted log-odds with an informative Dirichlet prior (Monroe, Colaresi & Quinn 2008).

All of the data, and short notebooks that reproduce the main results, live in this piece’s GitHub repository.
